record.paper_title: Recent advances and open questions in neutrino-induced quasi-elastic scattering and single photon production
record.original_question: How can the scaling analyses and short-range correlation information obtained from inclusive electron quasielastic scattering be made usable in neutrino-nucleus CCQE analyses, given that neutrino experiments generally do not know the incident neutrino energy event by event and therefore cannot directly establish the transferred momentum q and transferred energy ω?

evidence.quote:
Clearly a great deal relevant to neutrino–nucleus scattering has been learned
via the scaling analyses of inclusive electron QE scattering from nuclei. Such
measurements are feasible with electrons where the critical variablesq and ω are
readily obtained from measurement of the momentum of the scattered electron.
Unfortunately, for most neutrino experiments these quantities are out of reach.
Thus, scaling cannot at the moment be applied to neutrino experiments due to a
lack of knowledge of the incident neutrino energy which limits how well q and ω
can be established.

The appearance of short-range (high momentum) pairwise
correlations among 20% of the nucleons in a nucleus is especially important.
These correlations are known to be the cause of the enhancement appearing
in the nuclear transverse response. These correlations will be shown to be
important in neutrino-nucleus CCQE scattering.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. In inclusive quasielastic (QE) lepton–nucleus scattering, the kinematic variables of the reaction are the three-momentum transfer q and the energy transfer ω from the probe to the nuclear target. For inclusive electron QE scattering, both q and ω are determined event by event from the measured incident and scattered electron momenta, and the inclusive double-differential cross section, divided by an appropriate single-nucleon factor and expressed in a suitable scaling variable ψ(q,ω), exhibits "superscaling": the resulting scaling function f(ψ) becomes (to good approximation) independent of q and of the target nucleus. From these analyses one also extracts information about short-range correlated nucleon pairs (a high-momentum component carrying roughly 20% of the nucleons) that produce an enhancement in the transverse nuclear response.

For charged-current quasielastic (CCQE) neutrino–nucleus scattering νℓ + A → ℓ⁻ + X, the incoming neutrino energy Eν is not measured event by event; it is drawn from a broad flux Φ(Eν), and only the outgoing charged-lepton kinematics (and possibly hadronic observables) are recorded. Consequently q and ω cannot be reconstructed directly from the lepton kinematics alone, so the electron-scattering scaling function f(ψ) and the short-range-correlation information cannot be applied event by event in the standard way.

Problem. Devise a quantitative procedure that takes as input

  (i) the superscaling function f(ψ) and the associated transverse-enhancement contribution from short-range correlated pairs, as extracted from inclusive electron QE scattering data, and
  (ii) a known neutrino flux Φ(Eν) together with the measured outgoing charged-lepton (and, where available, hadronic) kinematics,

and produces predictions for flux-integrated CCQE neutrino–nucleus differential cross sections that consistently incorporate the electron-scattering scaling and short-range-correlation information despite the event-by-event ignorance of Eν, q, and ω. Specify how to fold the unknown Eν over Φ(Eν), how to treat the axial-vector response and the meson-exchange/2p2h contributions tied to short-range correlations, and quantify the residual theoretical uncertainty introduced by the unknown incident neutrino energy.
artifact.status_search_result: The SuSA and SuSAv2 programs (Amaro, Barbaro, Caballero, Donnelly, et al.) have extended electron-scattering superscaling to neutrino CCQE by folding the extracted scaling function over the neutrino flux and adding a 2p2h/meson-exchange-current contribution tied to short-range correlations. These approaches give working predictions for MiniBooNE, T2K, MINERvA and NOvA CCQE data, but residual flux-folding uncertainties and tensions in some kinematic regions remain, so the underlying question is partially addressed rather than fully closed.

status_evidence.title: Superscaling analysis of inclusive electron scattering and its extension to charged-current neutrino-nucleus cross sections (SuSAv2)
status_evidence.snippet: We present a new version of the SuSA model... applied to neutrino-nucleus CCQE scattering by folding over the neutrino flux.
status_evidence.claim: The SuSAv2 framework adapts electron-scattering scaling functions to neutrino CCQE despite unknown Eν.

status_evidence.title: Meson-exchange currents and quasielastic neutrino cross sections in the SuperScaling Approximation
status_evidence.snippet: We add a 2p-2h MEC contribution arising from short-range correlations to the SuSA neutrino CCQE prediction.
status_evidence.claim: Short-range-correlation information from electron scattering has been incorporated into neutrino CCQE predictions via 2p2h MEC additions.
